newsitem.title: GHANA: Ghana seeks bids for floating power station.
newsitem.headline: Ghana seeks bids for floating power station.

text.p: The Ghana National Petroleum Corporation (GNPC) will invite tenders from March 17 for building a Japanese-funded barge with gas-fired turbines, capable of generating between 85 and 125 Megawatts, GNPC said.

Project coordinator Ben Dagadu told Reuters that GNPC was also inviting tenders for building two 161kV overhead transmission lines (total 176 km), a new 225/161kV substation and the extension of an existing substation.
Japan's Overseas Economic Cooperation Fund had pledged 12.9 billion yen to finance the barge and the extension of the grid, he said. GNPC is to raise 4.0 billion cedis locally.
The barge, to be delivered in Q1 1999, is part of GNPC's ambitious floating power house project in a lagoon near the border with Ivory Coast.

Dagadu said a first barge with two 48 Megawatt turbines was being built by Westinghouse of Orlando, Florida. The $65 million barge is financed by the U.S. Maritime Administration. Commissioning of that barge is scheduled for Q4 1998.

Natural gas from Ghana's Tano oil and gas fields will fuel the barges. Proven reserves there are 287 billion cubic feet, of which 193 billion cubic feet is recoverable. Exploration continues, gas production facilities are yet to be put in place.
In the long run, the floating power house is to tap gas from an off-shore pipeline between Nigeria and Ivory Coast.

Tender documents will be on sale from March 17. Bidding closes at 1200 GMT on May 19. Details available from Ben Dagadu Tel: +233-22-204726 Fax: 232039/232053 or A.
